FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE

FIX #5015 (link existing issues this PR will resolve)

In this PR we implement typical acceptance sampling as one of the alternate sampling techniques for the Speculative Decoding verifier. In this sampling we do the following

  1. For every draft token we compare its probability in the target probability distribution with the entropy of the target distribution and if it meets the acceptance criteria then we accept it. More details on the acceptance criteria can be found in section 3.3.1 in this paper (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.10774)
  2. We stop at the first token that is rejected and return
  3. If no draft tokens are accepted then we use greedy sampling to sample a token from the target distribution corresponding to k = 0. The paper also specifies sampling as the fallback option in case no draft tokens are selected
  4. If all the draft tokens are selected then we append the bonus token to the end. The Medusa paper does not talk about the bonus token optimization. However we accept the bonus token since it is drawn from the same target distribution that we are using for accepting the rest of the tokens.

In this PR we make the following changes

  1. Add typical_acceptance_sampler.py which implements the sampling logic described above. Also added test cases for the new sampler.
  2. Create a base class spec_decode_base_sampler.py to be used by both the rejection_sampler and the new typical_acceptance_sampler.
  3. Move some of the logic from rejection_sampler into spec_decode_base_sampler such that it can be used by both the samplers.

As part of this PR we introduce the new sampler. We will hook it up into the spec_decode_worker in a later pr

One thing we should check is that typical acceptance latency is ~= rejection sampling latency (and not 2x+ or something).

I modified the test_spec_decode_e2e_greedy_correctness_tiny_model_large_bs in tests/spec_decode/e2e/test_multistep_correctness.py and ran it both with rejection_sampling and typical_acceptance sampling with 68m model as the draft and 160m model as the target. The latencies of both are similar.

Below is the sample Spec Decode metrics that I got from the run. The avg time is the time spent in the forward pass in the 2 samplers averaged across all invocations.

This statistics is for temperature = 0.5, output length = 256 and batch = 64

rejection sampling

INFO 06-06 06:38:06 metrics.py:362] Speculative metrics: Draft acceptance rate: 0.765, System efficiency: 0.576, Number of speculative tokens: 5, Number of accepted tokens: 18180, Number of draft tokens tokens: 23780, Number of emitted tokens tokens: 16447, Avg Time: 0.0017990445097287495.

typical acceptance sampling
INFO 06-06 06:40:24 metrics.py:362] Speculative metrics: Draft acceptance rate: 0.843, System efficiency: 0.610, Number of speculative tokens: 5, Number of accepted tokens: 18946, Number of draft tokens tokens: 22470, Number of emitted tokens tokens: 16437, Avg Time: 0.0014608523675373622

@sroy745 one question about this new sampler (relates to work in #6034): it seems to me that the forward method of TypicalAcceptanceSampler is deterministic with respect to its inputs. e.g., if repeatedly call forward with the same input, we would always get the same output. In contrast, this is not the case for the RejectionSampler which will produce differnet output each time. Is this the correct understanding? Thanks!

@tdoublep yes the TypicalAcceptanceSampler should be deterministic as opposed to the RejectionSampler. All the computation in the sampler is deterministic once the input is fixed.
